prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the design of long-acting incretin therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single B023 prize to Drucker, Holst and Knudsen. The round-1 exchange sharpened the reasoning rather than the outcome. The chair's central question is whether the core is the physiology, the drug design, or both. I answer both, because the physiology identified the target and the acylated, albumin-binding analogues showed that the target could be drugged for weeks at a time. Without the second step the native peptide, with a half-life of minutes, stays a laboratory observation. The outcome evidence is broad and independent (glycaemia, weight, cardiovascular and renal endpoints), the mechanism is stable, and no member disputes maturity. Five of six of us now name the same trio. I do not count that as evidence. Several of us said we may share assumptions about what counts as a therapeutic chain, so I tested the trio against the opposite assumption, a physiology-only prize. That version needs a third name whose claim does not rest on settling priority with Habener and Bell, and the supplied record does not give one. Knudsen's contribution is documented, specific and undisputed, so I keep her. A single achievement also avoids pairing GLP-1 with a second part whose credit is less settled.
statement.case_against: The credit gap remains real. Three names cannot cover Holst, Drucker, Knudsen and Mojsov, and Habener and Bell are outside the credited list altogether. A prize that credits a company-based scientist beside two academic discoverers can be read as rewarding optimisation. If the committee decides the prize is for basic discovery alone, my trio is the weaker one and Mojsov would be the better third name. That would need documented evidence that her identification of the active peptide was decisive, and I have not seen it. The citation I propose names the physiology and the long-acting design, and I accept that wording makes the compound character of the prize explicit. Wahren-Herlenius also raises long-term safety beyond weight and glucose, which is still being defined. I regard it as a caveat on the clinical record, not a reason to defer. B023 is also a large prize for a single year. If it were judged too compound, B051 is the alternative I can defend most quickly.

responses.point: Perlmann keeps Mojsov in the third place over Knudsen, on the ground that identification of the active peptide is upstream of every analogue, and would accept Knudsen only if the committee explicitly concludes the Mojsov record cannot be resolved.
responses.response: Your upstream argument is the strongest case for Mojsov and I take it seriously. Where I differ is on what a laureate seat can rest on. Your own ballot says her role is contested and that Habener and Bell are part of the same story. A seat that depends on that dispute is more fragile than one that depends on semaglutide and liraglutide. Since you ask for the decision to be explicit, I state it: I cannot resolve the peptide-identification priority from the supplied record, and I will not place a laureate on a contested claim for that reason. I would move to Mojsov only if someone documents that her work was decisive and not just early. I also accept your point that the citation should not overstate the discovery side, which is why my wording names the physiology and the long-acting design separately.

responses.point: Linnarsson moved Knudsen into his trio in place of Mojsov after rereading colleagues' ballots, on the view that acylated long-acting analogues are the step that turned the biology into medicine, while holding that a prize mixing physiology and industry may be read as compound or as favouring a company.
responses.response: I agree with the move. In round 1 I said I would accept Mojsov if the committee treated the prize as basic discovery, so your reasoning matters to me, and I think it settles the question. The Physiology or Medicine criterion is the benefit to humankind, and the acylation work is the step that made the benefit possible. I share your worry about the company reading. My answer is that the worry attaches to the citation and not to the person. Knudsen's contribution is a specific design solution with a named mechanism, and the citation should say so. I also note that you changed your view because of our exchange. That is a better sign than the first-round agreement, which could reflect shared assumptions. Your remaining unease about leaving out Mojsov is also mine. I do not think it should change the configuration.

responses.point: Svenningsson asks the committee to decide explicitly whether the prize rewards physiology, drug design or both, and argues that the combination is the core because the discovery established the target and the drug design proved it.
responses.response: I agree that the committee should decide this explicitly. My decision is the combination, with the two halves named in the citation as separate steps. I also take your comment that our agreement may not be independent. I tested it by asking what I would conclude if physiology alone were the criterion. I could not complete that configuration without choosing a side in the Mojsov, Habener and Bell dispute. So the combination is easier to defend in the record we have. On the one-versus-two question you raise, I do not think B023 needs a partner. Pairing it with B051 would give a clean second credit, but it would put a basic pathway discovery beside a clinical prize without a single rationale. B051 is a candidate for a later year, and I would want to see more direct disease evidence by then.

responses.point: El Manira argues that stabilising GLP-1 against DPP-4 and prolonging its action by acylation was a discovery-level insight, and defers on Mojsov only if the committee can document that her work was decisive.
responses.response: We are close on this. I agree that dropping the drug step would leave a prize about a hormone and not about the medicine that changed practice. I would add one point for the citation. The DPP-4 stabilisation idea belongs to the broader incretin-therapy story, and the acylation and albumin-binding design is Knudsen's contribution. The citation should describe the long-acting design without implying that every step of development is credited. On your disagreement with my low ranking of optogenetics, I accept the correction on significance. The channelrhodopsin mechanism is original and its reach is wide. My hesitation is about credit allocation among six claimants, and you make the same point when you decline to force three names this year. That is why I do not propose it as a second part.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius supports the Drucker, Holst and Knudsen trio, says the Nobel tradition has rewarded translational steps when the chain is clear and the contribution can be named, and adds that long-term safety of the class beyond weight and glucose is still being defined.
responses.response: I agree on the trio and on the tradition point. The translational step is rewarded when the individual contribution can be named, and here it can. Your safety caveat is the one reservation no one else raised, and I think it deserves a real answer. The mechanism is stable and the outcome evidence is broad, with trials running over a decade. Safety questions beyond weight and glucose are still being defined, but they concern monitoring of a widely used class, not whether the discovery holds. The committee has recognised drugs with continuing safety surveillance before. I would keep this as a stated uncertainty and would not treat it as grounds for delay. You said B028 is a credible later-year candidate and that is also my reading. I rank it second among alternatives because of the population-level evidence, and the adjacency to the 2008 HPV prize and the unresolved Zhou question keep it from the preferred configuration.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide was decisive. I cannot resolve her priority against Habener and Bell from the supplied record, and I would revisit the third name if someone documented it.
Whether the citation wording is enough to head off the reading that the prize favours a company, since it names two steps and three people from two different settings.
Whether long-term safety of the incretin class beyond weight and glucose changes the balance of the case. I think it does not, but the evidence is still accumulating.
Whether the near-unanimity of the committee reflects independent scientific judgement or shared assumptions about what counts as a therapeutic chain.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. My Karolinska Institutet affiliation and past co-authorship with Linnarsson and Frisen (single-cell and neurogenesis work, with the Linnarsson count not independently audited) do not concern any shortlisted candidate. I have no documented tie to the B023 names or to any other credited candidate, and I infer none from shared topics. I propose no recusal for myself or for the other members' disclosures, none of which involves a credited name.
